escena: SCENE (cinematic, Hollywood blockbuster still with real depth of field, epic scale, a vast dark cathedral-like studio at night): a Latin American creative director in her mid thirties, dark curly shoulder-length hair, wearing the Efeonce hoodie exactly as in its reference, stands slightly RIGHT of center in the lower part of the frame, framed from the waist up, looking straight into the lens with a knowing, amused half-smile. In her left hand she holds a half-used roll of matte black gaffer tape; with her right hand she presses the last strip of tape flat over the corner of a large glowing screen right beside her. REALISTIC ADULT PROPORTIONS: camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm at f/2, nothing foreshortened, she does not lean toward the lens. Around and behind her floats a constellation of EXACTLY SEVEN large luminous screens of different real formats at different depths: a tall vertical film frame, a website, a product box, a street billboard, a phone, a square social post and a poster. All seven belong to ONE fictitious brand with an unmistakable visual signature: the same bold, sweeping vivid orange (#FF6500) brushstroke shape, the same off-axis composition, the same deep navy grounds and the same grainy photographic texture, while each application does a different job. On EVERY screen, the corner where a logo would sit is covered with a strip of matte black gaffer tape, slightly wrinkled and real, and the brand is still instantly recognisable. DEPTH: the screen beside her is sharp, about one meter away; the others recede three to eight meters into the haze, progressively out of focus. LIGHT: the screens are the only light sources; the nearest screen throws warm orange light on her face, hand and hoodie, NO fill light, the far side of her face falls into soft shadow. A cool azure (#0375DB) rim light from behind outlines her hair and shoulders. Thin haze catches the orange glow. The TOP 30% of the frame is calm, deep dark studio space with only faint haze, no screens, no light, no objects; every screen stays below 34% of the frame height. Rich contrast, deep navy blacks, punchy color. No readable text, no letters, no logos of any brand anywhere.

lecho.objeto: the near-black matte edge of a long work table close to the lens across the whole bottom of the frame, completely out of focus, outside every light and every reflection

texto.muro: calm, deep dark studio space with only faint haze
